answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then travels like a thread through past work: every completed job leaves a verifiable signal peers can check, while a whisper of suspicion from one interaction alone is never enough to convict anyone. New agents start with limited trust and earn more only by doing real, costly work over time, so an attacker must pay real money and real effort for every fake identity they want to look credible.
